step1_analysis.description: A highly simplified track-and-hold or peak detector circuit consisting of a single diode and a hold capacitor. The capacitor charges to the peak of the input signal minus the diode's forward voltage drop and holds the value.

paper_reference.title: A Broadband 10-GHz Track-and-Hold in Si/SiGe HBT Technology

v_peak.description: Maximum steady-state output voltage (peak detected voltage)

sky130_expected.calculation: Input peak is 0.9V DC + 0.1V AC = 1.0V. Diode forward drop is approx 0.6V. V_peak = 1.0V - 0.6V = 0.4V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the exact saturation current (IS) of the diode model used. A standard silicon diode drops around 0.6V to 0.7V.

ripple.description: Peak-to-peak voltage variation on the hold capacitor during steady state

sky130_expected.calculation: Without a discharge resistor, the capacitor only discharges through the diode's reverse leakage current, which is extremely small (e.g., 1e-14 A).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Ripple should be near zero in this idealized passive peak detector without a load.

power_consumption.description: Average power drawn from the input source

sky130_expected.calculation: Passive circuit with no DC path to ground. Power is only consumed during the initial charging of the 325fF capacitor.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper's 550mW refers to the full active track-and-hold amplifier with buffers and current sources. This simplified passive netlist consumes negligible power.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure the peak detected voltage, steady-state ripple, and power consumption of the simplified track-and-hold circuit.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Peak Detector / Track-and-Hold Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameters
.param C_hold = 325f

* DUT (Corrected syntax for standard SPICE diode)
D1 IN OUT DMOD
Ch OUT 0 {C_hold}

* Generic Diode Model (since specific SKY130 diode isn't instantiated by name)
.model DMOD D(IS=1e-14 RS=10 N=1)

* Sources
VIN IN 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 SIN(0.9 0.1 1MEG 0 0)

* Analyses
.control
  * Run transient analysis for 5 cycles of 1MHz
  tran 10n 5u
  
  * Measure peak voltage in steady state (last 3 cycles)
  meas tran v_peak max v(OUT) from=2u to=5u
  
  * Measure minimum voltage in steady state to calculate ripple
  meas tran v_min min v(OUT) from=2u to=5u
  let ripple = v_peak - v_min
  print ripple
  
  * Measure RMS current to estimate power drawn from VIN
  meas tran i_rms rms i(VIN) from=2u to=5u
  let power_consumption = i_rms * 0.9
  print power_consumption
  
  quit
.endc
.end
